problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨-2,3,0⟩+t⟨3,-2,1⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨4,1,-3⟩=-19.
$$
worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨-2+3t,3-2t,t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-2+3t,3-2t,t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,1,-3⟩ & =-19 \\ ⟨-2+3t,3-2t,t⟩\cdot ⟨4,1,-3⟩ & =-19 \\ 4(-2+3t)+1(3-2t)-3t & =-19 \\ -8+12t+3-2t-3t & =-19 \\ 7t & =-14 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-2+3(-2),3-2(-2),(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,7,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-8,7,-2).$
